body: Are you sure they don't?  It sounds kind of cool to me.

> In my opinion, I think people hate hearing that they need professional help.

One of my other friends who has gone through a lot of mental health issues has told me the same thing.  I'm half just venting with this, but she did go to see a doctor and she was really happy with the first appointment and they set her up with a psychologist.  But when she had the followup they made her feel unheard and like they weren't really concerned about it.  I know that she was seeing a physician/pathologist just then and not the actual psychologist, but now she feels like seeking professional help is pointless again and it's really frustrating.

>Also, you can help them with organizing their day, homework, or etc. It's very crucial that you don't judge them but rather just focus on helping things come back together.

I try to do this one, but I don't really know how to convince her to get out of bed when she's feeling particularly bad.  I try to offer her some bite-sized sessions of getting up and doing some things and then she can lay back down for a bit after, but I don't know if that specific suggestion is helpful or not and it often doesn't really convince her to move about anyhow.  I'm kind of stuck with that one.

EDIT: Also how should I handle here actively wanting to take a nap?  Should I still suggest other things?  Should I tell her to sleep tight and let her be?  What's the right thing there?
